ggtt_hwsp_contract.status: source-verified address chain, breadcrumb command and cache-flush primitives; TLB effect and real completion unverified
ggtt_hwsp_contract.question: Does the GGTT address the GPU is told to write the completion seqno to reach the same bytes the CPU polls, and is the write command well formed on this port?
chain: i915_ggtt_offset(hwsp vma) is the GGTT virtual address of the pinned status page
intel_timeline.hwsp_offset = that offset (or a shared offset) plus the in-page seqno slot; intel_timeline.c:75-99 keeps hwsp_offset < hwsp->size
both sides therefore name the same in-page slot by construction, because the CPU pointer was built from the same offset the GPU command uses

anchors: drm: gt/intel_execlists_submission.c:3515-3521 rcs_submission_override, GRAPHICS_VER 12 -> emit_fini_breadcrumb = gen12_emit_fini_breadcrumb_rcs

drm: gt/gen8_engine_cs.c:812-853 gen12_emit_fini_breadcrumb_rcs emits PIPE_CONTROL (CS_STALL, TLB_INVALIDATE, TILE/RT/DEPTH flush, DC_FLUSH_ENABLE, FLUSH_ENABLE), adds FLUSH_L3 because IP_VER < 12.70, adds DEPTH_STALL for Wa_1409600907 because GRAPHICS_VER 12 and IP_VER < 12.55, then gen12_emit_ggtt_write_rcs(seqno, hwsp_offset(rq), 0, FLUSH_ENABLE|CS_STALL)
drm: gt/gen8_engine_cs.c:784-809 the gen12 tail adds MI_USER_INTERRUPT, the arb enable and the semaphore busywait
verified.finding: ADL-S is graphics version 12 and IP version below 12.55, so the RCS breadcrumb is the gen12 variant with L3 flush and depth stall, not the gen8 or gen11 one. The write is a PIPE_CONTROL qword store, not an MI_FLUSH_DW.

verified.edge: the write targets a global GTT address and must be 8-byte aligned
anchors: drm: gt/gen8_engine_cs.h:104-115 gen12_emit_ggtt_write_rcs asserts IS_ALIGNED(gtt_offset, 8) and ORs PIPE_CONTROL_GLOBAL_GTT_IVB
drm: gt/gen8_engine_cs.h:128-140 gen8_emit_ggtt_write (the non-RCS path) asserts the same alignment and clears bit 5 because MI_FLUSH_DW uses that bit
verified.finding: The seqno slot named by hwsp_offset is a global GTT address, so it resolves through the GGTT rather than the PPGTT. That is why the status page must be a GGTT vma; it also means the GGTT PTE for that page, reviewed on the DMA/PTE path, is what the GPU dereferences.

anchors: drm: gt/intel_timeline.c:64 pin_map is hardcoded I915_MAP_WB, not the per-platform coherent map type
drm: gt/intel_timeline.c:69-70 the slot is zeroed and then drm_clflush_virt_range is called so the GPU reads zeros
drm: gt/intel_engine_pm.c:85,88 reads it with READ_ONCE(*ce->timeline->hwsp_seqno)
drm: i915_request.h:611 i915_request_completed -> __i915_request_is_complete under rcu_read_lock, i.e. the completion decision is a plain seqno read of that mapping
verified.finding: The CPU polls a write-back kernel mapping with no explicit cache invalidate on the completion path, so observing the GPU's store depends on the shared LLC (has_llc = 1 for ADL-S). That is upstream i915's assumption for this page, not something the port changed.

verified.edge: cache-flush primitives actually execute on this port
anchors: drm: drivers/gpu/drm/drm_cache.c:166-189 drm_clflush_virt_range takes the CONFIG_X86 branch: static_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_CLFLUSH) then an mb()-fenced clflushopt loop with a final clflushopt(end-1), else wbinvd_on_all_cpus()
generated flags from experimental/uhd770/tools/gen_flags.py include -DCONFIG_X86, -DCONFIG_X86_64 and -DCONFIG_X86_PAT, so the CONFIG_X86 branch is the one compiled
freebsd: sys/compat/linuxkpi/common/include/asm/cpufeature.h:16-31 static_cpu_has(X86_FEATURE_CLFLUSH) tests cpu_feature & CPUID_CLFSH
port: override/include/linux/page.h:109-123 clflushopt becomes lkpi_clflushopt: CLFLUSHOPT when cpu_stdext_feature has it, else CLFLUSH, else pmap_invalidate_cache()
port: bsdcompat/include/machine/cpufunc.h:10-11 clflushopt and wbinvd are real instructions
port: override/src/linux_compat.c:2263,2325 boot_cpu_data.x86_clflush_size is set from cpu_clflush_line_size, so the loop stride is not zero
port: override/src/linux_compat.c:2033 linux_wbinvd_on_all_cpus is the rendezvous-based fallback
verified.finding: The flush is not a stub: the compiled branch issues real cache-line flushes with the required barriers, the line size is initialised from the CPU, and both weaker fallbacks exist. A zero line size, which would divide the loop, is excluded by the initialisation path.

verified.edge: the breadcrumb also carries a GPU-side TLB invalidate
anchors: drm: gt/gen8_engine_cs.c:816-822 PIPE_CONTROL_TLB_INVALIDATE is part of the same flush before the seqno write
verified.finding: The GPU invalidates its own TLB after the batch, so a stale PTE is not carried into the next submission by the GPU. The driver-side invalidation in intel_tlb.c is a separate path and is still open below.

verified.edge: driver-side full TLB invalidation before a page-table change becomes visible
anchors: drm: gt/intel_tlb.c:121-158 intel_gt_invalidate_tlb_full takes the GT runtime pm reference, serialises on gt->tlb.invalidate_lock and skips when a full invalidate seqno already passed

drm: gt/intel_tlb.c:49-111 mmio_invalidate_full holds FORCEWAKE_ALL, takes intel_gt_mcr_lock and uncore->lock only around the register writes, writes tlb_inv.request for each awake engine, applies Wa_2207587034 for adl-s by writing GEN12_OA_TLB_INV_CR = 1, releases both locks, and only then waits for completion

drm: gt/intel_tlb.c:30-47 the wait uses TLB_INVAL_TIMEOUT_US = 100 and TLB_INVAL_TIMEOUT_MS = 4 (intel_tlb.c:22-23), i.e. a 100us atomic poll then a 4ms sleepable wait, both below the 20000us assertion in intel_uncore.c:2738
drm: intel_engine_cs.c:1232-1243 tlb_inv.mcr is set only for the xehp register layout, so ADL takes the non-MCR path through __intel_wait_for_register_fw
verified.finding: The ADL-S workaround is present and the ACK waits are performed after both locks are dropped, so the 4ms sleepable wait is legal (might_sleep_if in intel_uncore.c:2737). The port only supplies the surfaces this path uses: uncached MMIO (verified above), usleep_range (linuxkpi delay.h:82), the audited spinlock, and the delayed-work put for forcewake. Whether the hardware clears the invalidate bit inside those windows is the target-only half.

open: whether the hardware completes the invalidation within the 100us/4ms windows is target-only

ppgtt_root_and_pde.status: source-verified parent PDE encoding and context root programming; page-walk, pin ordering and all hardware effects unverified
ppgtt_root_and_pde.question: Does the GPU reach the page tables the driver wrote: is every parent directory entry and the context root filled with the DMA address of the object it names, with the flags the hardware expects?
chain: child page-table and page-directory objects are i915 internal GEM objects; their pages are DMA-mapped by i915_gem_gtt_prepare_pages through the S/G -> BSD -> native path already reviewed
a parent entry is gen8_pde_encode(px_dma(to), I915_CACHE_LLC) written as one 64-bit slot and flushed (intel_ppgtt.c:98-110 via intel_gtt.h:643-649)
gen8_pde_encode ORs GEN8_PAGE_PRESENT and GEN8_PAGE_RW into the raw address and adds PPAT_CACHED_PDE for any cache level other than NONE (gen8_ppgtt.c:19-31)
the context root is px_dma(ppgtt->pd) split upper/lower 32 bits into CTX_PDP0_UDW and CTX_PDP0_LDW (intel_lrc_reg.h:40-45)

the 4-level branch is the one taken: i915_vm_is_4lvl is (total - 1) >> 32 (intel_gtt.h:425), and ADL-S is GEN12_FEATURES with __runtime.ppgtt_size = 48, so init_ppgtt_regs calls ASSIGN_CTX_PML4 rather than assigning four PDPs (intel_lrc.c:888-902)

verified.edge: no CPU physical address enters a parent entry or the context root
anchors: drm: gt/intel_ppgtt.c:109 __set_pd_entry passes px_dma(to) to the encoder
drm: gt/intel_lrc_reg.h:42 ASSIGN_CTX_PML4 reads px_dma((ppgtt)->pd)
drm: i915_gem_gtt.c:326-330 __px_dma returns sg_dma_address(p->mm.pages->sgl)
verified.finding: Both the parent entries and the context root come from sg_dma_address of the already DMA-mapped object. No page_to_phys, virt_to_phys or struct page field is used, so a device address and a CPU physical address cannot be confused on this path.

verified.edge: 64-bit address width preserved to the register pair
anchors: drm: gt/gen8_ppgtt.c:19-31 gen8_pde_encode takes dma_addr_t and returns u64, ORing flags into it
drm: gt/intel_lrc_reg.h:43-44 ASSIGN_CTX_PML4 splits with upper_32_bits and lower_32_bits
verified.finding: The address stays 64-bit from sg_dma_address through the encoder, and the context root is explicitly split into its upper and lower halves, so nothing is truncated to 32 bits on the way to the context image.

verified.edge: the entry is ordered before the GPU can walk it
anchors: drm: gt/intel_ppgtt.c:92-95 write_dma_entry stores the encoded 64-bit entry and calls drm_clflush_virt_range(&vaddr[idx], sizeof(u64))
drm: drivers/gpu/drm/drm_cache.c:167-189 the flush aligns down to the cache line, starts with mb(), issues clflushopt per line, then serialises with clflushopt(end - 1) and a final mb()
verified.finding: The store, the leading mb() and the line-aligned flush give a published parent entry before the context is submitted. On this port the flush is the real CONFIG_X86 branch recorded under ggtt_hwsp_contract.

verified.edge: the flags ORed into the address cannot collide with address bits
anchors: drm: gt/gen8_ppgtt.c:23 pde = addr | GEN8_PAGE_PRESENT | GEN8_PAGE_RW, plus PPAT_CACHED_PDE
drm: gt/gen8_ppgtt.c:19-31 no mask or alignment assertion in the encoder itself
verified.finding: The encoder ORs flags into the low bits of the address, so it relies on a 4K-aligned DMA address. That holds because the mapped objects are whole pages and the DMA path maps page-aligned ranges, but the encoder itself does not assert it. Worth an explicit assertion if this path is ever fed a non-page-aligned object.

open: pin ordering: that the top page-directory object already has pages and a DMA address at the moment init_ppgtt_regs reads px_dma (upstream guarantees it, this review has not traced the allocation-to-context-init order itself)
whether the GPU page-walk actually reaches the parent entries (target only)
scratch/TLB interaction when a parent entry is replaced or cleared while the GPU is using it

cpu_alias_cache_modes.status: source-verified alias encoding round trip, alias creation and flush primitives; real visibility and snooping unverified
cpu_alias_cache_modes.question: When the CPU writes through a kernel alias and the GPU reads the same page through DMA, do the two agree on the cache mode, and is there any place that asks for a mode change the port silently ignores?
encoding: cachemode2protval(attr) = (attr << LINUXKPI_CACHE_MODE_SHIFT) | LINUXKPI_PROT_VALID, shift 4, valid bit 1<<3 (override/include/linux/page.h:53-64)
pgprot_writecombine keeps VM_PROT_ALL and encodes VM_MEMATTR_WRITE_COMBINING (page.h:89-90); pgprot_noncached encodes VM_MEMATTR_UNCACHEABLE (page.h:86-87)
pgprot2cachemode returns prot >> 4 when the valid bit is set and VM_MEMATTR_DEFAULT otherwise (page.h:66-73)
the values in machine/vm.h are PAT encodings (UC 0x00, WC 0x01, WT 0x04, WB 0x06), so the decoded mode is also the value cache_option() switches on

verified.edge: single-page write-back mapping reuses the allocator's own alias
anchors: drm: gem/i915_gem_pages.c:302-303 I915_MAP_WB returns page_address(sg_page(...)) instead of creating a mapping
port: override/src/linux_page.c:85-90 linux_page_address returns page->nmx_kva
port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_page.c:206-213 page_prepare sets md.pat_mode = VM_MEMATTR_WRITE_BACK and zeroes through that same alias
verified.finding: For a single page the WB view is exactly the alias the allocator already has, so a CPU write and the zeroing done at allocation time are the same view.

verified.edge: multi-page write-back mapping lands on the cached default
anchors: drm: gem/i915_gem_pages.c:304-305,321 multi-page WB uses vmap(..., PAGE_KERNEL)
port: override/include/linux/page.h:66-73 PAGE_KERNEL carries no valid bit, so pgprot2cachemode yields VM_MEMATTR_DEFAULT
port: override/src/linux_page.c:378-386 vmap then substitutes pages[0]->md.pat_mode when the decoded mode is VM_MEMATTR_DEFAULT, which is WRITE_BACK for these pages
port: xnu/nmx_vm.cpp:21-28 VM_MEMATTR_WRITE_BACK (0x06) reaches the default branch and maps with kIOMapDefaultCache
verified.finding: WB does not accidentally become uncached: the default-prot branch falls back to the page's recorded attribute rather than to cache mode zero.

verified.edge: write-combined and uncached aliases decode exactly
anchors: drm: gem/i915_gem_pages.c:306-308 I915_MAP_WC uses pgprot_writecombine(PAGE_KERNEL_IO), and PAGE_KERNEL_IO is 0x0000 (page.h:58)
port: override/include/linux/page.h:89-90 pgprot_writecombine(0) = 0x18, decoding to VM_MEMATTR_WRITE_COMBINING (0x01)
port: xnu/nmx_vm.cpp:24-26 0x01 is NMX_CACHE_WC and maps with kIOMapWriteCombineCache; 0x00 is NMX_CACHE_UC and maps with kIOMapInhibitCache
verified.finding: The three modes i915 asks for (WB, WC, UC) map one-to-one onto the three IOKit mapping options, and the encode/decode round trip is exact for each.

verified.edge: two aliases of one page are expected, not accidental
anchors: drm: gem/i915_gem_pages.c:302-321 WB may return the allocator alias while WC always creates a vmap alias of the same pages
port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_page.c:706-710 pmap_page_set_memattr invalidates the kernel alias when a page leaves write-back
port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_page.c:693-696 pmap_change_attr returns 0 without changing any existing mapping
verified.finding: The allocator keeps a WB alias at nmx_kva and i915 may add a WC alias on top. Changing an existing alias is not what happens: i915 chooses the mode when it creates the mapping. The WB alias is only invalidated if the page's recorded attribute itself changes, which this path does not do.

verified.edge: the empty pmap_change_attr is reachable, but not from the i915 compute path
anchors: port: bsdcompat/src/nmx_page.c:693-696 pmap_change_attr returns 0 with no effect
freebsd: sys/compat/linuxkpi/common/include/linux/set_memory.h:88-118 set_pages_array_wb/wc/uc are built on pmap_change_attr
drm: drivers/gpu/drm/ttm/ttm_pool.c:183-202 ttm_pool_apply_caching calls set_pages_array_wc/uc under #ifdef CONFIG_X86, which gen_flags.py does define
grep over the pinned DRM tree: no i915 source calls set_pages_array_*, set_memory_* or pmap_change_attr
verified.finding: The stub is a real unimplemented behaviour: a TTM caller asking for WC or UC on existing pages is told it succeeded while nothing changes. It is off today's path because i915 selects the mode when creating the mapping, but it must not be cited as evidence that a mode change works.
